gp.text: The following table summarizes certain key sales statistics and percentage of gross profit for the three and six months ended May 3, 2025 and May 4, 2024.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses as a percent of net sales was 13% in the second quarter of 2025 compared to 17% for the second quarter of 2024 and was 13% for the first six months of 2025 compared to 15% in the first six months of 2024. Selling, general and administrative expenses in the second quarter of 2025 was $1,889,197 compared to $1,911,380 in the second quarter of 2024 and was $3,565,847 for the first six months of 2025 compared to $3,943,710 for the first six months of 2024. The dollar increase in expenses for the first six months of 2024 versus 2025 were due to increase in employee sales commission as a result of higher sales at our Company owned retail sales centers.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses as a percent of net sales was 13% in the second quarter of 2025 compared to 17% for the second quarter of 2024 and was 13% for the first six months of 2025 compared to 15% in the first six months of 2024. Selling, general and administrative expenses in the second quarter of 2025 was $1,889,197 compared to $1,911,380 in the second quarter of 2024 and was $3,565,847 for the first six months of 2025 compared to $3,943,710 for the first six months of 2024. The dollar increase in expenses for the first six months of 2024 versus 2025 were due to increase in employee sales commission as a result of higher sales at our Company owned retail sales centers.

net.text: We reported net income of $2,292,320 for the second quarter of 2025 or $0.70 per share, compared to $2,025,959 or $0.62 per share, for the second quarter of 2024. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Major Customers – There were no customers that accounted for more than 10 % of our total net sales in fiscal year 2025 or 2024.
Modular homes manufactured by Nobility are required to comply with the Florida Building Code established by the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulations.
We identified the estimation of manufacturing cost on homes manufactured by the Company that remain in inventory as a critical audit matter.

The Company’s limited warranty covers substantial defects in material or workmanship in specified components of the home including structural elements, plumbing systems, electrical systems, and heating and cooling systems which are supplied by the Company that may occur under normal use and service during a period of twelve (12) months from the date of delivery to the original homeowner, and applies to the original homeowner or any subsequent homeowner to whom this product is transferred during the duration of this twelve ( 12 ) month period.

s.t: Since all allocations are to be made on a 50/50 basis and the Company’s maximum exposure is limited to its investment in Majestic 21, management has concluded that the Company would not absorb a majority of Majestic 21’s expected losses nor receive a majority of Majestic 21’s expected residual returns; therefore, the Company is not required to consolidate Majestic 21 with the accounts of Nobility Homes in accordance with ASC 810.
As of November 1, 2025, we are not involved in any material unconsolidated entities (other than the Company’s investments in Majestic 21).
Investment in Majestic 21 – Majestic 21 was formed in 1997 as a joint venture with our joint venture partner, an unrelated entity, 21 st Mortgage Corporation (“21 st Mortgage”).
With regard to our investment in Majestic 21, there are no differences between our investment balance and the amount of underlying equity in net assets owned by Majestic 21.
